reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about surface energies, segregation behavior, diffusion kinetics, and high-temperature stability in a complex multi-element system, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific segregation and stabilization behavior of 1–2 at.% Pt in a Fe–Co–Ni–Cu–Al nanoparticle under the stated extreme conditions.
premises: Pt has a lower surface energy than the other elements in the HEA nanoparticle
This lower surface energy drives Pt surface segregation at low bulk concentrations (1–2 at.%) during synthesis
A Pt-enriched surface layer reduces atomic mobility and limits diffusion of other elements
Reduced atomic mobility prevents phase separation and preserves near-equiatomic internal composition
This stabilization persists under high-temperature catalytic (773–1173 K) and thermoelectric (473–1923 K) conditions
